rules.explain: PARIS is pah-REE (no S). PETIT is puh-TEE (no T). Read the middle, drop the tail.

rules.rule: Nasal vowels hum through the nose
rules.explain: ON (bon), AN (enfant), IN (vin) hum like a blocked nose. BON = boh(n) — don't pop the N!
Gargle a soft R at the back: ROUGE = rroozh. Never roll it Spanish-style.

rules.rule: U vs OU are different sounds
rules.explain: OU = oo (LOU). U = tight lips, say EE: RUE (street) vs ROUE (wheel). Round your lips hard!
French leans forward: BONJOUR = boh(n)-ZHOOR, MERCI = mair-SEE. The end is always strongest.

alphabet.title: The French alphabet: 26 letters
alphabet.explain: Same letters as English, but the NAMES sound French. Learn them to spell your name aloud: JE M'APPELLE … (my name is …), ÇA S'ÉPELLE … (it is spelled …).

letters.tip: S, or Z between vowels: ROSE

counting.title: Counting 0 to 100
counting.explain: Learn 0–16 by heart. 17–19 = DIX + number (dix-sept). 20–69 are regular (trente-deux). Then the famous twists: 70 = 60+10, 80 = 4×20, 90 = 4×20+10!
rules: 80 = quatre-vingts (4×20): drops S when followed: quatre-vingt-deux = 82.

lessons.title: Bonjour! Greetings and politeness
lessons.learn: BONJOUR works all day until evening, then BONSOIR. SALUT is hello/bye for friends. Magic trio: S'IL VOUS PLAÎT (please), MERCI (thanks), PARDON (sorry). AU REVOIR closes every meeting.

grammar.title: Every noun is LE or LA (un/une)
grammar.explain: Masculine nouns take LE/UN, feminine take LA/UNE. Learn every noun WITH its article: LE livre, LA maison. No shortcuts — gender is half the word!
mistakes: Saying LA livre — livre is masculine: LE livre.
Skipping articles (saying just Maison) — always LE/LA/UN/UNE.

grammar.title: ÊTRE: je suis, tu es, il/elle est
grammar.explain: JE SUIS = I am, TU ES = you are, IL/ELLE EST = he/she is. French always keeps the pronoun (JE, TU, IL) — never drop it like Spanish!
grammar.pattern: je suis · tu es · il/elle est
mistakes: Dropping JE (saying SUIS Léa) — French needs JE SUIS.
Saying IL for a woman — she is ELLE.

lessons.learn: Meet the family: MÈRE, PÈRE, FRÈRE, SŒUR. Age uses AVOIR (to have): J'AI DIX ANS = I have 10 years = I am 10. Ask: TU AS QUEL ÂGE? (You have what age?)

grammar.title: AVOIR for age: j'ai… ans
grammar.explain: J'AI = I have, TU AS = you have, IL/ELLE A = he/she has. Age: J'AI + number + ANS. TU AS QUEL ÂGE? = How old are you?
mistakes: Saying JE SUIS dix ans — age always uses AVOIR.
Saying AN without S: ANS sounds ahn — keep the S silent!

lessons.title: Food and -ER verbs
lessons.learn: Food first! EAU, PAIN, LAIT, POMME. Order with JE VOUDRAIS (I would like): JE VOUDRAIS UN CAFÉ. Most verbs end in -ER: PARLER → JE PARLE, TU PARLES, IL PARLE (all sound the same: parl!).

grammar.title: Present -ER: je parle, tu parles, il parle
grammar.explain: Drop -ER, add -E, -ES, -E. All three sound the same (parl)! Spelling differs, sound doesn't. PARLER, MANGER, AIMER — hundreds of verbs, one music.
mistakes: Pronouncing the -S in TU PARLES — silent! All sound parl.
Saying PARLE without JE — French keeps its pronouns.

lessons.title: Colors and adjectives
lessons.learn: Adjectives match gender AND usually come AFTER the noun: LA MAISON BLANCHE (the white house). Most add -E for feminine: ROUGE stays, but BLANC → BLANCHE, NOIR → NOIRE.

grammar.title: Adjective agreement: add -E for feminine
grammar.explain: LE livre ROUGE, LA maison ROUGE (rouge never changes!). But: BLANC → BLANCHE, NOIR → NOIRE, PETIT → PETITE. Plural adds silent -S: LES livres ROUGES.
mistakes: Saying LA maison BLANC — feminine needs BLANCHE.
Putting colors before the noun (English order) — after!

lessons.title: Days, months, and telling time
lessons.learn: Days are lowercase and masculine: LE LUNDI. Time: QUELLE HEURE EST-IL? Answer: IL EST TROIS HEURES. Half: ET DEMIE — IL EST TROIS HEURES ET DEMIE.

grammar.title: Telling time: il est… heures
grammar.explain: IL EST UNE HEURE (1:00), IL EST DEUX HEURES (2:00). Half: ET DEMIE. Quarter: ET QUART. Always HEURE(S) — never drop it!
grammar.pattern: il est + number + heure(s) (+ et demie)

examples.t: Il est trois heures et demie.
examples.r: eel eh trwah zurr eh duh-MEE.

mistakes: Saying IL EST TROIS (no HEURES) — always add HEURES.
Capitalising days (Lundi) — French days are lowercase.
